Create a contact matrix according to individual contact rates

Source: R/make_random_contacts.R
make_random_contacts.Rd

This function creates a contact matrix where individuals are allowed to have different contact rates. By default, it returns a number of contacts in a day, drawn from a Poisson distribution, but it can also return the presence/absence of contacts.

Usage

make_random_contacts(n, rate = 0, binary_output = FALSE)

Arguments

n

A single integer indicating the number of individuals in the population.

rate

A numeric vector on length n indicating the daily rate at which each individual makes contact with other individuals. If provided as as single number, this will be recycled. Defaults to 0 - no contact.

binary_output

A logical indicating the output should be presence/absence (TRUE), or numbers of contacts per day (FALSE, default).

Value

An n x n matrix of contacts, either number of contacts (default), or as presence/absence of contact (binary_output = TRUE). Sources are in rows, recipients in column.

Author

Thibaut Jombart

Examples

## 4 individuals, no contact with rate = 0
res <- make_random_contacts(4, 0)
res
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    0    0    0    0
#> [2,]    0    0    0    0
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    0    0    0    0

## same with higher rate
res <- make_random_contacts(4, 2.5)
res
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    0    2    1    0
#> [2,]    1    0    3    1
#> [3,]    1    0    0    0
#> [4,]    0    1    0    0

## 6 individuals with some Poisson-distributed heterogeneity in rates,
## average 5.6 contacts per day, except for indiv 2 (rate 500) and 3 
## (rate (0)) 
rates <- rpois(6, 5.6)
rates[2] <- 500
rates[3] <- 0
set.seed(1) # only to compare results with next example
res <- make_random_contacts(6, rates)
res
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    0    0    1    3    0    0
#> [2,]  103    0   93   87  101  108
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    1    0    0    0    1    3
#> [5,]    3    1    0    0    0    0
#> [6,]    3    0    2    2    2    0

## same, binary output (fixing seed for comparable results)
res_nb <- res
set.seed(1)
res <- make_random_contacts(6, rates, TRUE)
res_nb
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    0    0    1    3    0    0
#> [2,]  103    0   93   87  101  108
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    1    0    0    0    1    3
#> [5,]    3    1    0    0    0    0
#> [6,]    3    0    2    2    2    0
res 
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    0    0    1    1    0    0
#> [2,]    1    0    1    1    1    1
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    1    0    0    0    1    1
#> [5,]    1    1    0    0    0    0
#> [6,]    1    0    1    1    1    0
